title: Incident Flagline: Quickstart Strip & Compact Brief prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: On-call responders and engineers land in long incident pages and often miss the most important triage signals (SLO delta, recent cost spikes, postmortem link). The current alert header is tall and noisy; it takes multiple clicks to find the runbook or to grab a compact summary for handoff. Goal: Design a compact "Flagline" — a single-line, persistently docked strip at the top of an incident thread that surfaces critical signals, enables one-click runbook/postmortem linking, and provides a compact handoff card that can be copied/shared. This ticket contains the prototype, design rationale, accessibility notes, interaction animations, and a review log.
acceptance_criteria: Flagline prototype in Figma with desktop and mobile states (collapsed/expanded)
Compact brief payload that copies to clipboard with markdown-compatible fields (title, SLO delta, top-3 logs, postmortem link)
Design spec for telemetry events (open, copy-brief, escalate, attach-postmortem)
Accessibility pass: keyboard focus, high-contrast variant, screen reader labels
Implementation checklist aligned with ENG-28945 and PM-1327: API surface for SLO delta and cost snapshot
decisions: Keep Flagline single-line by default; expand on hover/click to reveal quick actions (3 max) to reduce cognitive load
Display SLO delta as a sparklined percentage with color-coded delta chip rather than full graph to save real estate
Expose 'Copy Compact Brief' which generates a markdown snippet that includes a permalink, top-3 log excerpts (first 120 chars), SLO delta, and suggested next steps
Defer embedding runbook content; provide an 'Attach Runbook' flow that opens a focused modal and does not preload long content for perf reasons
Mobile: collapse Flagline into an overflow kebab with preview badge to avoid consuming vertical space on phone screens
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Initial discovery — interviewed 6 on-call engineers and SREs. Common asks: one-click postmortem linking, quick copy for handoffs, and a clear SLO delta visible without scrolling.
2026-03-01 - Luca Martinez: First pass prototypes available in Figma. Link in attachments. Included two variants: 'chip-first' and 'context-first'.

2026-03-03 - Product review (Anika Patel): Prefer 'chip-first' because it surfaces SLO delta consistently. Requested adding a cost delta microbadge for incidents tied to autoscaling or batching regressions.

2026-03-04 - Engineering feedback (from ENG-28945 sync): Need compact API that returns SLO delta, cost_snapshot, and canonical_permalink. Also need a feature flag to gate experiments for 10% of orgs. DEPENDENCY: implement feature flag in the control plane before rollout.

2026-03-06 - Accessibility review (Raul Gomez): Keyboard focus order and ARIA labels look good. Recommend increasing hit target for the Copy Brief action to 44px and ensuring the expanded brief is announced when copied.

2026-03-08 - Design review meeting notes: Added micro-interaction animations for copy confirmation and a subtle pulse when SLO crosses a configured threshold. Decided to limit quick actions to: Copy Brief, Attach Postmortem, and Escalate (with suggested assignees).

2026-03-09 - Prototype user test (5 participants): Copy Brief was used successfully by 4/5; one user suggested preset templates for different responder roles. Action: add 'templates' follow-up subtask if adoption metrics justify it.

2026-03-10 - PM sign-off (Anika Patel): Good to ship to rollout A/B with feature flag. PM requests telemetry events to capture Copy Brief usage and whether copied payload included postmortem link. Added to acceptance criteria.
follow_up_tasks: Create ENG subtasks for API endpoints (SLO delta, cost snapshot) and feature flag integration
Add templates sub-issue for responder-role brief presets (DES-?)
Plan 2-week A/B rollout with telemetry (events: flagline_open, copy_brief, attach_postmortem, escalate_click)
Prepare a short how-to snippet for oncall rotation emails and internal runbook
notes_for_engineering: Telemetry: include incident_id and user_role in events. Avoid PII in copied briefs. Use server-side render of markdown permalink to avoid client URL mismatch.
Performance: flagline must not block initial incident render; request lazy fetch for log excerpts and cost snapshot with 250ms timeout fallbacks
Security: postmortem links may be gated by org permissions. Design should handle 403/404 with graceful inline state and 'Request Access' CTA
